title: docs: add Mike versioning and historical snapshots
description:
## Why

DSPy currently publishes one mutable Material-for-MkDocs site. Users cannot select documentation for the exact DSPy version they installed, and replacing the deployment discards previous generated API documentation.

This PR solves version storage without changing renderers: Current and all bootstrapped releases remain Material builds. The Zensical migration is the next, independently reviewable PR.

## What this PR does

- adds official Mike 2.2.0 as the Git-backed version store;
- establishes `/current/`, immutable `/X.Y.Z/` snapshots, and redirect-only `/X.Y/` aliases;
- lists Current and every archived stable or prerelease snapshot in the picker while hiding minor aliases;
- reconstructs stable 3.0.0–3.3.1 releases and 3.4.0b1 from their tags using the original Material pipeline;
- installs the exact PyPI wheel for API introspection (`3.1.1` is tag-built because it was never published);
- records source, artifact digest, renderer, dependency, and optimization provenance;
- refuses automated replacement of a differing existing release snapshot;
- bootstraps one complete Material candidate—history plus Current—on `krypticmouse/dspy-docs:versioned-docs`;
- keeps existing deep links working with `/api/` → `/current/api/`-style redirects;
- scopes hand-authored root-relative links to their selected version;
- applies the shared compact release picker styling to Current and historical builds.

## What is live

- **When this DSPy PR merges:** `dspy.ai` remains the legacy Material site, and ordinary docs pushes continue updating it exactly as they do today. There is no stale-production window.
- **After the manual bootstrap:** only the non-production `versioned-docs` branch contains the complete versioned Material candidate.
- **After its deployment-repository PR is reviewed and merged:** the versioned Material site becomes live on the existing Vercel project/domain. The DSPy workflow detects `versions.json` and thereafter publishes Material Current through Mike to production `master`.

Before that deployment PR merges, create `legacy-material-backup`. Rollback restores that tree with a normal reviewed commit; no Vercel branch or project switch is required.

## Version and storage model

| URL | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `/` | redirect to `/current/` |
| `/current/` | mutable Material build from `main` at this stage |
| `/X.Y.Z/` | stable snapshot built from that tag and released artifact |
| `/X.Y.ZbN/` | prerelease snapshot; does not claim the stable minor alias |
| `/X.Y/` | redirect to the newest imported stable patch in the minor line |

Mike stores completed HTML, assets, search indexes, redirects, and `versions.json` in the existing deployment repository. Serving an old snapshot requires neither MkDocs nor its historical Python environment. Browsers fetch only the selected page and assets, not the aggregate Git repository.

## Historical fidelity

The old docs toolchains were not present in `uv.lock`; each tag had a separate, incompletely pinned `docs/requirements.txt`. Bootstrap replaces its moving DSPy dependency with the release artifact, resolves the remaining requirements no later than the tag timestamp, and records the complete result. The fidelity contract is routes, anchors, content, notebooks, matching API symbols, redirects, search, metadata, navigation, and interactions—not byte-identical HTML from an environment that was never archived.

## Visual review

The only intentional visual changes in this PR are the shared compact release selector (**magenta**) and consistent desktop search treatment (**cyan**). Historical pages otherwise retain their tag's Material rendering. URL redirects, immutable storage, provenance, and deployment activation are non-visual.

### Current Material site

The picker exposes Current and every archived release, including 3.4.0b1; minor aliases remain hidden redirect targets.

![Current Material site with the new version picker and shared search treatment boxed](https://ampcode.com/user-content/artifacts/350a593a3068dee12735312e80774ff145b5511c6f060bf69b2f617a63374164-file.png)

### Historical Material snapshot

Selecting a release changes the selected label and keeps the same picker/search treatment on the stored tag-built site.

![Historical 3.3.1 Material snapshot with the version picker and shared search treatment boxed](https://ampcode.com/user-content/artifacts/55cef3951de36551945bf465e85d544c89dd9fc937be7a94ea5d9b964713f7c4-file.png)

### Newly released 3.4 beta

The beta is independently selectable but does not create `/3.4/`; that alias begins with the stable release.

![The new 3.4.0b1 picker row boxed](https://ampcode.com/user-content/artifacts/a23bf5e010836505d034b018293ab63d9cc8a603b8ac8555bca03140af09f218-file.png)

## Safety and maintenance

Release snapshots are immutable to automation: an identical retry is a no-op and a differing retry fails. A deliberate correction is a reviewed PR against the affected directory in `krypticmouse/dspy-docs`; Git history supplies audit and rollback.

Bootstrap publishes only after all requested snapshots and Material Current have built locally. The live updater chooses legacy or Mike behavior from production's actual `versions.json`, so this PR is independently mergeable before the deployment cutover. Its legacy push is a normal optimistic Git update: if the Material/Mike promotion lands concurrently, the legacy push is rejected and leaves the promoted tree intact.

## Validation

- 9 focused docs/versioning tests pass, including 8 version-store tests against official Mike 2.2.0;
- tests cover patch preservation, alias movement, immutable replacement refusal, mutable Current, root/deep-link redirects, stale redirect removal, Vercel static configuration, and version-scoped root links;
- Ruff, formatting, Python compilation, workflow YAML parsing, and `git diff --check` pass.

## Stack

1. **This PR:** Mike versioning and historical Material bootstrap
2. [#10316](https://github.com/stanfordnlp/dspy/pull/10316): native Zensical Current with explicit compatibility adapters
3. [#10317](https://github.com/stanfordnlp/dspy/pull/10317): automate Current and future stable or prerelease snapshots
4. [#10332](https://github.com/stanfordnlp/dspy/pull/10332): remove one-time migration routing

bugs.summary: The vercel.json the publisher writes into the deployment repository only sets framework: null, trailingSlash and a header rule; it does not override the build command or the output directory, so the existing Vercel project keeps its legacy MkDocs build settings, rebuilds the old source tree and serves that instead of the Mike tree committed at the repository root. After the cutover the site shows the legacy homepage while /versions.json, /current/ and /X.Y.Z/ return 404.
bugs.trigger: Publish Current through Mike to the deployment repository served by the existing Vercel project (whose project-level settings still build the legacy MkDocs site) and request /current/ or /versions.json.
